title: Componentry 1.0.2
description: Fixes the Inspector emptying whenever a component chip is picked after leaving play mode. An editor that dies while the scene is reloading leaves its box behind in the Inspector's list and every box after it was counted one place out, so boxes are matched to the object each one is editing rather than to their place in the list now, and the bar is rebuilt on a play mode change instead of being left pointed at components the reload has replaced.

title: MiHordeAnimation 0.3.2
description: Fixes a body walking indefinitely while playing its idle clip: the locomotion manager caches which clip it believes each body is on, and an attack ends by crossfading into a return clip that manager never chose, so a body that attacked while walking came out on the attack's idle with the cache still saying walk and nothing left that could notice. Adds ForgetClip, which the attack manager calls whenever it plays and which is worth calling alongside any direct one-shot of your own, plus the package meta files 0.3.1 was missing.

title: MiHordeAnimation 0.3.0
description: Adds the locomotion half the attack manager's own notes said was missing: one manager gives a whole crowd an entrance, an idle, a walk, a run and a death, chosen from how fast each body is actually moving, measured from how far its transform travelled rather than asked of whatever is moving it, so flow field bodies, NavMeshAgent bodies and anything a game moves itself are all driven the same way. Only bodies whose clip should change ever reach the main thread, two throttles bound how often the crowd is looked at and how many clips one check may start, and idle, walk, run and death are lists a body picks one variant from and keeps across all four, so its idle and its walk belong to each other.

title: MiHordeTraffic 0.7.1
description: Fixes the advisor arguing against the one setting that makes a fine grid affordable, to exactly the people who had just changed it. It claimed congestion walks every cell every frame, which stopped being true when that pass became a sparse active set, and it fired on the cell count alone however small the crowd was, while the report two lines below said three cells tracked; the session report also leaves out the technique comparison when no benchmark ran, rather than opening with four not run lines that read as something having failed, and counts bodies at their peak instead of at quit, where a pooled crowd is mostly asleep and every per body figure came out measured against the one enemy left standing.

title: MiHordeTraffic 0.7.0
description: Fixes HordeSpawn.TryFind and HordeFlowMovement.TryGetState throwing when called from anywhere but a narrow part of the frame: both read arrays the movement jobs own from Update until LateUpdate, which is where coroutines, events, button callbacks and wave timers all run, and the first body always landed because there was no work in flight yet to collide with, so the second spawn looked like the thing that had broken it. Adds CompletePending for anything reading those arrays itself, and two samples, a flow field crowd and a NavMeshAgent crowd, kept deliberately separate so whichever one is opened is the whole of what that technique costs to set up.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.6.3
description: Adds IsPlayingOnce on the animator, whether a one-shot is still running. Anything driving clips in bulk needs it: a crowd manager picking idle, walk or run from how fast a body is moving has no other way to tell that the body is part way through an attack or a death, and without it the gait cuts the one-shot off on the next frame the speed changes.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.6.2
description: Drops the requirement that a model carry an Animator to be baked, which had rigs getting an empty one added purely to get past the check. What sampling actually needs depends on the clip: a generic clip drives transforms by path and needs only the hierarchy those paths address, while a humanoid clip carries muscle curves retargeted through the rig's Avatar and an Avatar is reached through an Animator, so only the second case asks for the component now, and where one is needed it goes on the throwaway copy the baker was already making rather than onto the model on disk.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.6.1
description: Fixes the baker window failing on every repaint after the package is updated while it is open. The window carries its state across an assembly reload by serializing it, and updating the package is a reload where the code reading that state is not the code that wrote it, so a list that arrived missing threw inside OnEnable and the console then filled with one GUI error per repaint, all describing the same failure and none of them naming it; the restore drops a snapshot it cannot read now and says so once, and Tools > MiVertexAnimation > Reset Baker Window does the same on demand.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.6.0
description: Adds clips straight from the project, dropped onto the Animation section or picked with the object field beside it, instead of only the ones read off the target's Animator Controller. Libraries of downloaded animation ship one clip per file, so a character with forty of them meant forty states in a controller that nothing would ever play, wired up purely so the baker could see them, and a model with no Animator at all can be baked now; a clip authored for a different hierarchy is named in the list rather than baked into a row of identical frames, and a model with Mesh LODs is no longer reported as having none, which it was because the level count was the fewest any mesh in the bake carried and a 55 vertex jaw runs out long before an 899 vertex body.

title: MiHordeTraffic 0.6.0
description: Adds HordeTarget, which gives a goal a shape of POINT, BOX or SPHERE with its size read from a Collider, so the expansion seeds every walkable cell the shape covers rather than the single cell nearest its centre and a crowd arrives at the nearest part of a building and surrounds it instead of funnelling onto one face. Fixes obstacles never applying at all on a large grid, where a block request waited for a frame with no expansion in flight and a million cell grid never has one, so a building switched off never came back for the rest of the session; bodies with no route to the goal hold position now rather than walking at it, since a straight line at the goal is not a route and the reason there is no route is usually something solid on exactly that bearing.

title: MiHordeTraffic 0.5.0
description: Adds gates. An obstacle is SOLID or GATE, and a gate stays walkable so the expansion still reaches through it at a great price while the mover refuses the step, which is what leads a crowd to a shut door and holds them queueing there instead of pressing them against whatever lies between, as likely to be a mountain as the door; height is part of what a step costs now, since the bake had sampled a height per cell from the beginning and nothing had ever read it, with a Maximum Slope above which two cells stop being connected at all, and separation's frame counting interval becomes Updates Per Second so one asset gives the same crowd at sixty frames and at two hundred.

title: MiHordeTraffic 0.4.0
description: Fixes the grid inventing walkable ground around everything solid in the level, and bodies standing inside walls on it: the bake asks the navmesh for the nearest surface to each cell centre and that call answers however far away it has to look, so a cell centre buried in a wall found the navmesh at the wall's foot and was accepted. Adds Sample Accuracy on the driver for how closely a cell has to sit on the navmesh to be baked as walkable, and fixes the field pulling bodies into walls once a route filled up, where an uphill neighbour on one side and a wall on the other read as the wall being the cheaper way.

title: MiHordeTraffic 0.3.0
description: Moves the field expansion off the main thread. It is scheduled, runs across however many frames it needs and is promoted when it finishes, so a million cell grid stops being a hitch every rebuild interval and the crowd reads the previous field while the next one is built; the congestion pass now walks the cells the crowd is standing in rather than the whole map, which was fifteen million memory bound operations a frame on a kilometre at one metre, and the per cell direction array is gone, a million entries written every expansion of which a crowd of five thousand ever read five thousand. Adds HordeObstacle and HordeMovingObstacle, which take the ground under them out of the grid and give it back with no re-bake, and HordeSpawn.TryFind, which answers where a body can actually be put down.

title: MiHordeAnimation 0.2.0
description: Fixes attack range being measured from the target's centre, so a crowd pressed against the wall of a large target stood half its width out of range and never swung. It is measured from the nearest part of the target now, taking the shape from HordeTarget where there is one and from the driver directly when this is chasing the same target the crowd is; a target with no shape is a point, exactly as before.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.5.0
description: Adds a name of your own for every baked clip, so a Play call can say Attack where the FBX exported Combat_Walk_1H_Attack. Renaming the clip on the importer was the only way to shorten that before and it changes the name for every other user of the file, while this is stored on the clip's range and survives a re-bake, an undo and a settings asset saved and loaded again; the baked clip set gets an inspector of its own for fixing a name without re-baking a texture to change a string, and both it and the baker warn when two clips would bake under the same name, since Play matches the first slice of a name and the second could only ever be reached by its index.

title: Multi-Platform Builder 1.10.0
description: Adds the text of every error and warning Unity logged to the build report, on a tab of its own with Errors Only and Copy Log beside it. This is what a failed build was missing: every platform switch reloads the domain and Unity clears the console with it, so with Switch Platform Per Build on the errors that explain a failure were wiped by the switch to the next platform and the report only ever kept the count, which left building that platform again by hand without the package as the only way to find out what broke.

title: MiHordeAnimation 0.1.0
description: Drives MiVertexAnimation clips from a MiHordeTraffic crowd out of one manager, rather than a script on every body measuring its own distance to a target. Bodies register once and are never dispatched again: a transform job and a Burst scan hand back only the handful whose animation should change, so a crowd of thousands standing still costs nothing at all, and the proximity attack it ships with plays a clip on every body that comes into range and sits out a cooldown.

title: MiHordeTraffic 0.2.0
description: Fixes the two signals the crowd steers on that had never once reached anything. The stall timer was cleared and read back in the same frame, so a body could only settle by standing inside the arrive radius - the one case the stall path exists to replace - and the unobstructed speed ramp that congestion prices progress against sat at about a tenth of a walking pace, so every jam on the map measured as flowing perfectly. Adds an overlap tolerance that gives separation somewhere to stop instead of churning forever, and a phases table in the session report that attributes main thread time stage by stage: the first thing it was used for said a 30 ms frame at 5000 bodies was 2.4 ms of crowd and the rest a prefab that had lost its LODGroup.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.4.1
description: Fixes the animator driver walking off its own list whenever a one-shot finished into a clip with no events on it, which is to say whenever an ordinary attack-back-to-idle call completed. Registering and unregistering are a subscript rather than a scan now, so joining the driver and dropping out cost the same whatever else is playing, instead of growing with the square of the crowd once thousands of bodies all start an attack.

title: MiHordeTraffic 0.1.0
description: Replaces per-agent A* with one flow field expansion that serves the whole crowd, and prices every cell by how fast bodies actually cross it, so a jammed route becomes expensive and a second one opens without anything having to notice the jam or decide a detour is worthwhile. Measured at 5000 bodies it holds a 12.08 ms mean frame against NavMeshAgent's 18.68 ms, and ships a runtime switch back to stock agents so that comparison can be rerun rather than believed.

title: MiHordeCrowd 1.0.0
description: Adds the parts a horde needs beyond pushing agents apart. Agents settle once enough of the neighbours ahead of them have settled, so a pack converging on one target comes to rest instead of grinding against itself, a detour steer sends agents stuck behind a jam around it rather than queueing, and repathing is paced by distance to goal so the ranks about to reach the player update far more often than the ones still crossing the map.

title: MiHordeFlow 0.2.0
description: Replaces NavMeshAgent's built-in local avoidance with a reactive separation pass running as a Burst job on the worker threads. Agents keep the NavMeshAgent for pathing and are pushed apart by a clamped force proportional to how far they overlap, so a crowd squeezing through a doorway compresses and relaxes instead of snapping, and groups let flyers, melee and slow ranged run different planes and update intervals in one scene.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.4.0
description: Adds hold points and speed control to playback. An animation can now freeze or stop on a given frame instead of looping straight back, so an enemy that falls stays down on its last frame for as long as you want. Clip speed is settable globally or per clip, which lets one character run faster without touching the timing its idle and attack were authored at.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.3.1
description: Fixes the shader clock drifting out of sync during Play mode when scene loads are swapped, which left animations reading from the wrong point in the bake.

title: DeadWeight
description: Rescue civilians and recruit them to your team, then unlock their traits to find out who is worth keeping. Some traits are hidden and some are bad, so the team you build is the risk you take. Made for Brackeys Game Jam 2026.2 on the theme 'Trust No One'; the jam build is still closer to a survival shooter than the full recruitment loop.

title: MiPackages
description: A hub for every package I maintain, in one Unity window. Each row shows the version the project currently has, an Add button for the ones it does not, and a Manage button that jumps straight to it in the Package Manager.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.3.0
description: Adds a Demo sample, importable from the Package Manager: a crowd scene with a character that turns to follow an orbiting target, a CC0 rig to bake it from, and all four section-driving modes on one component - point it at your own baked prefab and the scene demonstrates that instead. Samples now live in Samples~ so they stop compiling in every project that installs the package, and the baker no longer confuses two clips that share a name, which used to make frame ranges and events written for one overwrite the other's.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.2.0
description: Adds an LOD Group section that bakes the source mesh's own LOD levels into a single prefab, so a crowd keeps GPU instancing and still drops vertex work at distance - every level shares one texture set, because they share a vertex buffer. The prefab's mesh now also holds the baked pose, so a shader that is still compiling draws the character standing still instead of its bind pose at whatever scale the source file was authored in.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.1.0
description: Adds Reset Bake to the bake settings panel, which puts clip selection, frame ranges, events, sections and output settings back to their defaults without touching anything already written to disk. The bake settings asset also moves onto the Source row, behind a button that marks itself when a settings asset is loaded, instead of taking a section at the top of the window.

title: MiVertexAnimation 1.0.0
description: Bakes a SkinnedMeshRenderer and its animation clips into textures, so a crowd animates entirely on the GPU with no Animator, no bones and no per-frame skinning. The baker window previews the result before committing to a bake, places animation events on a track, and can leave a region of the mesh - a head, a torso - still drivable from script afterwards.

title: Componentry 1.0.1
description: Fixes component copying: the copy button is disabled with a reason when only the Transform is picked, Paste Rotation accepts a rotation copied from the Inspector's own Rotation field, and the button icons resolve wherever the package is installed. Entering Play mode with Reload Domain disabled no longer leaves stale state behind, and adding a component from a locked Inspector puts it on the object the bar is showing.

title: Componentry 1.0.0
description: Puts a row of buttons at the top of the Unity Inspector, one per component. Click one to show only it, search components by name, and drag to reorder or copy them between objects.

title: Multi-Platform Builder 1.9.2
description: Adds Android and WebGL to the platform list, with optional per-build platform switching so scripting symbols resolve correctly. Build reports now compare against previous builds and drill down by folder.

title: Multi-Platform Builder 1.1.0
description: Adds build reports that break the finished build down asset by asset, sorted by size, so the textures and meshes eating the most space are obvious before you start optimizing.

title: Spline Modular Kit 1.0.1
description: First public release of the spline based level building tool. It assembles authored modular art along a spline without deforming it, finds the real corners from the path, and keeps UVs correct by construction.

title: Meshes Hub 1.0.0
description: A mesh workbench that lives inside the Unity editor. Combine selected meshes into a single asset, strip the vertices and faces you do not need, and lay out new UVs without leaving the editor.

title: Mi Prefabs Painter 1.1.0
description: Paints prefabs onto whatever surface you are looking at in the Scene view, snapping and rotating every instance to the face it lands on.

title: Cold Rush
description: A short low-poly time attack racer. You get 15 seconds to finish the race, and freezing the clock is how you buy yourself more.

title: MiLocalization 1.0.0
description: JSON driven localization for Unity. Add a text key from an editor window and the strongly typed data class is generated for you, ready to use in code.

title: Multi-Platform Builder 1.0.1
